## Summary

The bug was in line 22 of `counter.py`: the condition `last = self.count == self.modulus` was comparing against an impossible value, since `self.count` is constrained to the range [0, modulus-1]. The fix changes the condition to `last = self.count == (self.modulus - 1)` so that the wrap signal correctly pulses when the counter reaches its maximum value (modulus-1) before wrapping back to 0.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug in the `GrayToBin` class was that it was computing each binary bit as the XOR of only two adjacent Gray code bits, when it should compute each bit as the XOR of all Gray code bits from that position to the MSB (i.e., `bin[i] = bin[i+1] ^ gray[i]`).

**Fix:** Changed line 31 in `hwlib/gray.py` from `bits[i] = self.gray[i + 1] ^ self.gray[i]` to `bits[i] = bits[i + 1] ^ self.gray[i]` to correctly accumulate the XOR result from the MSB down to each position.

Perfect! The bug is fixed.

## Summary

The ALU's SUB operation was computing `b - a` instead of `a - b` on line 31, causing 10 - 3 to incorrectly return 249 (which is -7 in two's complement truncated to 8 bits) instead of 7; I fixed it by changing the operand order from `self.b - self.a` to `self.a - self.b`.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the ALU's ADD operation carry flag calculation: it was checking bit 7 of the 9-bit result instead of bit 8 (the actual carry-out bit), causing false positives for sums with bit 7 set but no overflow (like 100 + 50 = 150) and missing actual overflows (like 200 + 100 = 300).

The fix was to change line 29 in `hwlib/alu.py` from `m.d.comb += self.carry.eq(wide[7])` to `m.d.comb += self.carry.eq(wide[8])` to correctly check the carry-out bit.

Perfect! All tests pass. The bug was in line 33 of `hwlib/fifo.py` where the `full` signal was incorrectly checking `self.level == self.depth - 1` instead of `self.level == self.depth`.

## Summary

The bug was caused by the full condition checking `level == depth - 1` instead of `level == depth`, causing the FIFO to report full when only 3 out of 4 entries were filled, which then prevented the 4th write.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the frame construction on line 28 of `hwlib/uart.py`: the data bits were being bit-reversed with `self.data[::-1]` when they should have been sent as-is. Since the transmission mechanism shifts the frame right by one bit each cycle and always sends `frame[0]`, the LSB is naturally sent first without any reversal needed. Removing the `[::-1]` bit-reversal operator fixes the issue, so `0x01` is now correctly transmitted as `0x01` (not `0x80`), and `0xA5` is correctly transmitted as `0xA5`.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in line 26 of `hwlib/pwm.py` where the comparison operator was changed from `<=` (less than or equal) to `<` (less than) to correctly implement the PWM duty cycle—the output should be high for exactly `duty` cycles per period, not `duty + 1` cycles.

Excellent! All tests pass now.

## Summary

The bug was in the `Debouncer` class's `elaborate` method. When the raw input matched the output state, the code was keeping the count the same (`count.eq(count)`) instead of resetting it to 0 (`count.eq(0)`). This allowed the counter to maintain its value even when the input bounced back to match the output, causing the debouncer to eventually register a press even when the input never stayed high for the required number of consecutive cycles. The fix resets the count to 0 whenever the raw input matches the current output, ensuring that the debouncer properly restarts its count on any bounce.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `Crc8Byte.elaborate()` method in `hwlib/crc.py`. The implementation was checking the least significant bit (`c[0]`) instead of the most significant bit (`c[7]`) to decide when to apply the polynomial XOR during the CRC calculation. Fixed by changing `Mux(c[0], ...)` to `Mux(c[7], ...)` to correctly match the standard CRC-8 algorithm behavior.
